text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A leading leftist party leader says an Islamist deputy who made a fiery speech condemned by the secularist establishment has revealed the true face of the ruling Islamist Welfare Party.
- Businessmen in the southeastern city of Diyarbakir attack their colleagues from western Turkey for all talk and no action after a meeting on overcoming poverty in the southeast.
- The military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) heavily criticises Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan at a meeting to discuss government implementation of anti-Islamist measures.
- The managing director of a leading state bank appointed by Islamist Erbakan sacks leading female officials at the bank.
- Military commanders give Erbakan a last warning at the NSC meeting about his failure to put their pro-secularist demands into practice.
- The coalition partners are unable to agree on a date for an early election, with Islamists seeking polls in October and the conservative wing of the coalition favouring an election in March.
- Public sector workers in an area of western Turkey gain the right for full pay when they make Moslem pilgrimages to Mecca.
- Military commanders criticise President Suleyman Demirel for failing to take the threat of Islamist activism seriously.
- Coalition partners to announce today that Ciller will take over the premiership in mid-June before going to elections in October.
- The National Security Council warns politicians that an election or a change of government will not weaken its will to push through a crackdown on a revival Islamist activity.
